Definition: to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent
BiblicalUsage: This verb is about willingness — to consent, to yield, to be agreeable. Isaiah promises, 'If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land'; Moses forbids Israel to consent to an enticer to idolatry; and Pharaoh, again and again, 'would not let them go'.
TheologicalSignificance: Willingness is where obedience starts, and Pharaoh shows what happens when it hardens into refusal. I believe God deals with the will first — His promise in Isaiah is conditional on a willing heart — and I would rather be willing and obedient than right and stubborn.
